programme: ATF6 sits at the top of this set as the transcriptional arm of the ER unfolded-protein response (HSPA5, XBP1, DNAJB9, PDIA6, CREB3, MANF, SYVN1, ATP2A2 among its targets), and TP53 sits downstream as the checkpoint that turns unresolved ER/proteotoxic stress into arrest or apoptosis (CDKN1A, GADD45A, BAX, CCNG1 among its targets). Together they describe a sense-then-decide proteostasis axis: ATF6 reads folding load in the ER, TP53 decides whether the cell repairs or dies.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease, ER stress from misfolded/aggregated protein (amyloid-beta, tau) chronically engages the ATF6 branch of the UPR; the retrieved material places ATF6 directly in AD ER-stress and proteostasis contexts (lipid peroxidation/ferroptosis, small-molecule ER proteostasis regulators, autophagy under oxidative/APP-driven stress). TP53's role here is asserted only via a multi-target systems-biology/simulation paper, not a dedicated AD mechanistic study.
role_in_b: In esophageal cancer, TP53 is one of the most frequently dysregulated genes, appearing across epidemiological risk-factor, autophagy-network, immunomodulatory, and prognostic-biomarker studies in the retrieved set. ATF6/ER-stress signaling is placed in esophageal cancer through a paper on ER stress in antitumor immunity and immunotherapy resistance, consistent with tumor cells leaning on UPR output to survive proteotoxic and immune stress.
shared_axis: A chronically stressed neuron and a proliferating tumor cell both have to manage ER folding load, and ATF6 is the sensor that reports it; TP53 is the checkpoint that converts that report into arrest/death or, when dysregulated, into survival. The same sensor-checkpoint pair could plausibly be pushed toward neuronal loss when chronically over-activated in AD and toward stress tolerance/immune evasion when blunted or rewired in esophageal cancer.
reasoning: Each factor is independently and repeatedly documented in one of the two diseases (ATF6 in AD ER-stress biology, TP53 in ESCC dysregulation), and the UPR-to-apoptosis module is nameable from their target genes alone, so this clears 'supported' rather than 'unexpected'. But no retrieved paper studies ATF6 or TP53 across both diseases jointly, the AD-side TP53 citation is a multi-target simulation paper rather than a dedicated mechanistic study, and the EC-side ATF6 citation concerns ER stress generally rather than the ATF6 branch specifically — so the cross-disease link is built by reasoning, not by anything retrieved, keeping this at 'moderate' rather than 'strong'.
support: PMID 40221538 (ATF6/ER-stress-linked lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis in an AD-relevant pathway) — places ATF6 in AD; PMID 41586813 (ER proteostasis regulator compounds, AD context) — places ATF6 in AD; PMID 39134286 (oxidative stress/autophagy deficits under mutant APP, ER-proteostasis framing) — places ATF6 in AD; PMID 42046149 (ER stress in antitumor immunity and immunotherapy resistance) — places ATF6/UPR in cancer including esophageal cancer; PMID 42353021 (systems biology/atomistic simulation of multi-target modulation in Alzheimer's disease) — places TP53 in an AD-relevant multi-target context, ambiguously; PMID 42645687 (epidemiological risk factors and inferred p53 pathway dysregulation in ESCC) — places TP53 in esophageal cancer; PMID 42204123 (autophagy-centered gene networks, prognostic biomarkers in esophageal cancer) — places TP53-associated network in esophageal cancer; PMID 42184060 (immunomodulatory mechanisms in esophageal cancer treatment) — places TP53-associated network in esophageal cancer; PMID 42556130 (TIIC prognostic tool for esophageal adenocarcinoma) — places TP53-associated network in esophageal cancer.
how_to_falsify: In an AD model (amyloid-bearing mouse or APP-mutant iPSC-neurons) and in ESCC cell lines, pharmacologically or genetically inhibit ATF6 and measure induction of the TP53 targets present in this set (CDKN1A, GADD45A, BAX, CCNG1) under proteotoxic stress. If the shared-axis account holds, ATF6 loss should blunt TP53-target induction and the downstream phenotype (reduced neuronal death in the AD model; altered stress-survival/chemosensitivity in ESCC) in both systems; if TP53-target induction is uncoupled from ATF6 activity in either system, the proposed sensor-checkpoint coupling is wrong for that disease.
caveats: Brain and esophagus are very different tissue and cell-biology contexts, and the 184 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 3 independent cohort pairs, so the effective statistical independence behind the recurrence counts is much lower than 184 suggests. The single-view exclusions (IRX3, HNF4G, ZNF256, etc.) show that many high-scoring factors were subgroup artifacts, which is why only broadly recurrent factors like ATF6 (110/184) and TP53 (125/184) are used here. The tissue-generic exclusion list (SOX10, ZEB1, NOTCH1, etc.) does not include ATF6 or TP53, so this module is not simply a generic-tissue regulator masquerading as disease-specific. ER stress/UPR is itself a broad, near-ubiquitous cellular stress pathway, so its specificity to this particular disease pairing — rather than to stressed tissue in general — is limited, and no retrieved paper studies ATF6 or TP53 jointly across AD and esophageal cancer.
